messages:
liu: heads up — want to sync on a small RFC follow-up: canonical root id for usage provenance. thinking about how upstreams should emit tokens/events so attribution + audits are unambiguous.

maria: +1. we've had ambiguity with duplicate tokens and late-arrivals. what's your proposal?

liu: idea A: every request gets a client_root_id (opinionated, generated by caller) and we append a server_root_id at ingest. attribution uses client_root_id if present, falls back to server_root_id.

josh: downside: callers forget to set client_root_id and some SDKs will generate opaque ids per retry, which breaks grouping. also trust boundary — we can't rely on client ids for billing integrity.

raj: for audits we need a single canonical id that we can trace across retries, handoffs, and backfills. can we canonicalize by (client_root_id || deterministic-hash(request_payload + timestamp-window))?

liu: thought about deterministic hashing too. sketch: server_root_id = sha256(client_root_id || request_signature || day_bucket). For pure server-only requests, server_root_id = sha256(request_signature || day_bucket).

maria: pseudo event example: ```json
{
  "server_root_id":"8a3f...",
  "client_root_id":"user-req-42",
  "tokens":123,
  "model":"redwood-v1",
  "ts":"2024-04-18T12:01:02Z"
}
```

josh: looks fine. couple of policy questions: 1) shard key — do we shard by server_root_id? 2) dedupe window size.

liu: propose shard by server_root_id prefix to keep attribution colocated. dedupe window: 5 minutes for interactive requests, longer (1h) for batch ingestion with idempotency markers.

raj: what about late-arriving logs for auditing? we need to reconcile without double-charging. suggestion: billing pipeline should emit provisional credits and final credits after finalization step; audits must reference final credits only.

maria: finalization event idea: once provenance finalized we emit a finalization record: `{type: "FINALIZE", server_root_id:..., final_tokens: ...}` then downstream connectors can reconcile.

ingest-bot: reminder: existing downstream connectors expect append-only events. introducing FINALIZE will require consumers to treat some messages as authoritative. please coordinate changelog.

josh: operationally, fallback behavior: if FINALIZE absent after X days, run auto-finalize using latest seen state and mark audit-warning. We should surface that to the console.

liu: also want an audit-mode header for sensitive customers: if enabled, upstreams must supply client_root_id and we persist full request_signature for traceability (encrypted-at-rest).

maria: encryption/KMS integration makes sense. store only hashed signatures for normal customers to save PII.

raj: question on backfills: if we backfill old events, do we emit FINALIZE with a backfill_flag? audits need to treat those differently to avoid altering historical billing.

liu: yes — backfill_finalization should carry backfill_ts and origin="backfill"; billing reconciler must treat origin priority lower unless customer explicitly accepts adjustment.

josh: vague edge: what about multi-tenant shared requests where a single request yields tokens for multiple tenants? server_root_id should remain the same but attribution granules must include tenant_id per line item.

maria: agreed. store event envelope: server_root_id + list[{tenant_id, tokens, attribution_key}]. makes rollups easier.

raj: next steps — liu to write a short RFC addendum with: canonical id generation, shard key plan, FINALIZE semantics, backfill policy, encryption note. we'll review Wed sync.

liu: will do. adding TODO: validate with SDK teams about client_root_id format and automatic generation in retries.

maria: thanks. small ask: include examples of old broken patterns we've seen (retry-per-call generating new client ids) so SDK fixes are targeted.

josh: :thumbsup:
